original_question: Let f run over holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight k_f <= T. Prove asymptotic formulas, with the best possible error terms, for the third and fourth moments of the central values L(1/2, f), normalized by L(1, ad f), in particular aiming for sums of the shape T^2 P3(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(1+epsilon)) for the cubic moment and T^2 P6(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(4/3+epsilon)) for the quartic moment.
target_in_paper: Problem (11) in the section "Problems" under "Moments of the Riemann zeta function": prove third and fourth moment asymptotics, with the stated optimal error terms, for central values L(1/2,f) over holomorphic Hecke eigenforms with weight k_f <= T, normalized by L(1, ad f).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly identifies the same family (holomorphic Hecke eigenforms in the weight aspect), the same central values L(1/2,f), the same normalization by L(1, ad f), and the same two target asymptotic shapes with main terms T^2 P_3(log T) and T^2 P_6(log T) and error terms O_epsilon(T^(1+epsilon)) and O_epsilon(T^(4/3+epsilon)).
missing_details: State explicitly that this is the paper's open Problem (11), not a theorem or conjecture proved there.
Quantify the asymptotic regime: the formulas are sought as T -> infinity, and the error terms are for every epsilon > 0.
Make explicit that P_j(x) denotes some polynomial of degree j; in particular, P_3 has degree 3 and P_6 has degree 6.
Define k_f as the weight of f.

To make the question fully stand-alone, specify the family being summed over more precisely: holomorphic Hecke cusp eigenforms, with one representative per Hecke eigenspace; the paper itself leaves the level implicit.
Clarify that L(1, ad f) is the adjoint L-value used as the harmonic normalization.
Say that this is only the weight-aspect problem; no level variation, twists, smoothing, or shifted moments are part of Problem (11).
Replace the phrase "best possible error terms" by the exact target exponents 1 and 4/3, since that is how Problem (11) formulates the goal.
refined_question: As T -> infinity, let f run over holomorphic Hecke cusp eigenforms of weight k_f <= T (in the full-level weight-aspect family intended by the paper), with one Hecke-normalized representative for each eigenspace. Prove that for every epsilon > 0 there exist polynomials P_3 and P_6 of degrees 3 and 6 such that sum_{k_f <= T} L(1/2,f)^3 / L(1, ad f) = T^2 P_3(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(1+epsilon)) and sum_{k_f <= T} L(1/2,f)^4 / L(1, ad f) = T^2 P_6(log T) + O_epsilon(T^(4/3+epsilon)). Here k_f denotes the weight of f and L(1, ad f) is the adjoint L-value.
justification: This draft is essentially a paraphrase of Problem (11) on page 7. The paper explicitly asks for third and fourth moment asymptotics for L(1/2,f) as f runs over holomorphic Hecke eigenforms of weight k_f <= T, normalized by L(1, ad f), and it explicitly states the two target asymptotic formulas with main terms T^2 P_3(log T) and T^2 P_6(log T) and error terms O_epsilon(T^(1+epsilon)) and O_epsilon(T^(4/3+epsilon)). The same sentence specifies that P_j is a polynomial of degree j. The final comparison with the Hecke-Maass case shows that the intended scope is precisely this holomorphic weight-aspect moment problem, not a broader automorphic-moment question. Problem (11) itself leaves the level implicit; the surrounding Humphries problems treat the analogous Maass family at level 1 and nearby weight-aspect families of primitive forms of level 1, so making the full-level interpretation explicit is a contextual sharpening rather than a broadening.
